html:
Suriname became independent from the Netherlands on 25 November 1975. In the years around independence about a third of its people moved to the Netherlands.

Many feared for their future in a new state divided between Creoles, Hindustanis and Javanese, and Dutch citizenship was about to end for those who stayed. Prime Minister Henck Arron led the country to independence with a large Dutch aid package, but the exodus continued after the coup of 1980.

Today some 350,000 people of Surinamese origin live in the Netherlands, more than half as many as in Suriname itself, mostly in Amsterdam, Rotterdam and The Hague. They have shaped Dutch football, music and food, and money sent home is important to Suriname's economy.
sum: Suriname became independent from the Netherlands on 25 November 1975. In the years around independence about a third of its people moved to the Netherlands.
